query_snapshot: Which alloy and heat-treatment conditions does NASA SP-8119 identify as susceptible to stress corrosion in its material-compatibility discussion?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- NASA SP-8119 lists alloy 2014 in heat-treated conditions T4 and T6 as susceptible to stress corrosion. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- NASA SP-8119 lists alloy 2024 in heat-treated conditions T3, T4, and T351 as susceptible to stress corrosion. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- NASA SP-8119 lists alloy PH15-7Mo in heat-treated conditions RH950 and TH1050 as susceptible to stress corrosion. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- NASA SP-8119 lists alloy 17-7PH in annealed and H900 conditions as susceptible to stress corrosion. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- NASA SP-8119 lists alloy 17-4PH in heat-treated conditions RH950 and TH1050 as susceptible to stress corrosion. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- NASA SP-8119 lists alloy AM350 in condition SCT850 as susceptible to stress corrosion. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- NASA SP-8119 lists alloy AM355 in condition SCT850 as susceptible to stress corrosion. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
- NASA SP-8119 states that materials susceptible to stress corrosion should not be used. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
